extracted.intended_audience: vehicle technology researchers, industry partners, national laboratories, and potential DOE VTO collaborators or applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Vehicle Technologies Office (VTO) priorities and standards for R&D and deployment of efficient, sustainable transportation technologies — describing what VTO supports, desired outcomes, and metrics/examples of impact. Useful for organizations seeking to align projects with VTO goals or to partner with the office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of supported activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vehicle Technologies Office supports research, development (R&D), and deployment of efficient and sustainable transportation technologies that will improve energy efficiency, fuel economy, and enable America to use less petroleum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologies called out include advanced batteries and electric drive systems, lightweight materials, advanced combustion engines, alternative fuels, and energy efficient mobility systems. Projects should relate to improving efficiency, economy, or reducing petroleum use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target technology areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority technology domains include advanced batteries, electric drive systems, lightweight materials, advanced combustion engines, alternative fuels, and energy efficient mobility systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and collaborations that advance these specific technology areas align with VTO priorities and are more likely to be relevant to the office's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with industry and labs
rubrics_metrics.description: VTO collaborates with industry leaders through partnerships like U.S. DRIVE and 21st Century Truck to accelerate technology development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships should accelerate development of highly efficient combustion engines and fuels, lightweight materials, and advanced batteries and electric drive systems, and should help identify opportunities to maximize mobility while minimizing energy impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance by technology roadmaps and clear targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and development is guided by technology roadmaps and with clear goals and technical targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should reference or align with VTO technology roadmaps and explicitly define technical targets and milestones. The page points to 'technology roadmaps' and 'clear goals and technical targets' as central organizing principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on commercialization and deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: VTO-funded R&D aims to enable adoption and commercialization of new technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The office highlights 'success stories' where VTO-funded research led to commercialization; proposals that demonstrate a credible pathway to market deployment and commercialization are consistent with VTO objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable energy and petroleum savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be able to demonstrate measurable reductions in petroleum consumption and improvements in fuel efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives quantitative examples: potential national savings of up to 3.1 million barrels per day (18% of U.S. petroleum consumption by 2035), and SuperTruck program examples (50% fuel efficiency improvement → 260 million barrels/year; 100% → 400 million barrels/year). Applicants should be prepared to estimate and justify projected energy/fuel savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain vehicle safety, performance, and power
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency improvements must maintain the safety, performance, and power of today's vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should ensure that gains in fuel economy do not compromise vehicle safety or expected performance characteristics; proposals should address how they will preserve or improve these aspects while increasing efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer and economic benefits articulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should articulate benefits to consumers and the U.S. economy, such as reduced fuel costs and support for domestic manufacturing and competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page quantifies household savings (example: improving from 20 to 30 mpg saves about $600/year at $2.36/gal) and highlights downstream economic advantages (lower operating costs for fleets, competitiveness, potential price impacts). Proposals should include estimates of consumer and economic impacts where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy security outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: VTO priorities include improving U.S. energy security by reducing reliance on imported petroleum and increasing resilience to oil price shocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that replace oil with domestic alternative fuels or substantially reduce petroleum consumption support national energy security goals and should make this case in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and public health impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing transportation emissions (greenhouse gases and nitrogen oxides) is a stated objective; projects should contribute to lowering emissions to protect public health and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites transportation accounting for more than 26% of GHG emissions and 57% of NOx emissions; proposals should quantify anticipated emissions reductions and discuss public health/environmental benefits where applicable.
